articles.title: In 1862, Abraham Lincoln signed a law that gave Americans a chance to claim 160 acres of free land. What happened next transformed the American West forever
articles.description: In 1862, President Abraham Lincoln enacted the Homestead Act, granting land to settlers eager to populate the West. This initiative allowed qualified individuals to claim 160 acres after five years of cultivation, significantly altering America's landscape. However, it also resulted in the displacement of Indigenous populations. The act prevailed for over a hundred years, leaving a lasting impact on the country's growth and development.

articles.title: A colder fridge setting is not always better; adjusting it by 1°C could reduce energy use by 8 to 11%
articles.description: Lowering your refrigerator’s thermostat beyond what’s required can lead to excessive energy usage. Opening the fridge door often hardly affects energy consumption, but by optimizing the fridge's location and setting, you can effectively reduce your electricity bills.

articles.title: Iran Missile Tactics Catch U.S. Off Guard; Air Defences Including THAAD Exposed; ‘Target Destroyed’
articles.description: A New York Times report reveals how Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) refined its missile and drone tactics to exploit weaknesses in U.S. air defences during the recent conflict.
